incident.title: Invoice exports receive quota responses after a route change
incident.description: Invoice export requests stopped being accepted after traffic moved to a different provider tenant profile.

evidence.summary: The rollout changed invoice provider tenant profile 8 to profile 12.
Every invoice export submitted through profile 12 returns HTTP 429 before a provider job ID is created.

references.title: Invoice provider tenant operations manual
references.content:
# Invoice provider tenant operations manual

## Request path

Invoice exports leave the export API only after validation, account lookup, and document rendering complete. The provider connector then selects a tenant profile. A successful provider submission returns a job ID before the export API begins polling. If no job ID exists, later polling and document-download behavior cannot explain the failure.

## Profile ownership

Profile 8 is the ordinary interactive tenant. Finance operations owns its billing relationship, and the export service uses it for customer-triggered invoices. Profile 9 is reserved for nightly archive work. Profile 12 belongs to the low-volume migration tenant used during controlled data moves. Route configuration, rather than invoice account identity, selects one of these profiles.

## Retries and timeouts

The connector retries HTTP 408 and selected HTTP 5xx responses twice. It does not retry HTTP 429 because the provider counts rejected retries against the same quota window. A timeout after a provider job ID is created belongs to polling. A response before job creation belongs to submission. These two stages have separate alerts and should not be combined when diagnosing an incident.

## Credentials

All three tenant profiles currently use valid client credentials. Authentication failures return HTTP 401 and include credential_error in the connector details. Credential rotation does not change quota allocation. Profile selection also does not change worker count in the export service.

## Capacity record

Profile 8 permits 20,000 invoice submissions per UTC day. Profile 9 permits 5,000 archive submissions per UTC day. Profile 12 permits 200 submissions per UTC day. The migration job consumed profile 12's full daily allowance at 08:40 UTC on 2026-08-20. Requests routed to profile 12 after that time receive HTTP 429 before the provider creates a job. The allowance resets at 00:00 UTC. Moving interactive exports back to profile 8 restores the intended quota boundary after approval.

## Interpretation rule

Use the selected profile, response status, and job-creation stage together. HTTP 429 on profile 12 before job creation after 08:40 UTC indicates exhaustion of the migration tenant's daily submission allowance. It does not establish a provider-wide outage, an export-worker backlog, or a credential failure.

references.title: Invoice export retry and polling guide
references.content: Invoice polling begins only after the provider returns a job ID. Polling timeouts can delay completed documents, while HTTP 408 and selected HTTP 5xx submission failures receive two retries. HTTP 429 is not retried. Retry policy does not increase a tenant quota and cannot create a provider job when submission was rejected before a job ID existed.

references.title: Invoice export worker capacity
references.content: Eight export workers render invoice documents. A worker backlog is present only when the render queue grows and healthy worker count falls below eight. Provider responses received after rendering do not measure worker capacity.

incident.title: Receipt callbacks fail signature verification after a slot change
incident.description: Signing receipts reach the callback service but fail verification after the verifier moved to key slot B.

evidence.summary: The verifier changed active receipt key slot A to slot B while retaining key revision 17.
Receipt callbacks signed with slot B revision 18 are rejected because the verifier loaded revision 17.

references.title: Receipt verification key inventory revision 18
references.content: Revision 18 is active from 2026-08-20. Slot A continues to use receipt key revision 17 during the overlap period. Slot B uses receipt key revision 18. A verifier selecting slot B must load revision 18 before accepting callbacks. Loading revision 17 in slot B rejects valid revision-18 signatures.

references.title: Receipt verification key inventory revision 17
references.content: Revision 17 was active until 2026-08-20. Slot A uses receipt key revision 17. Slot B also used receipt key revision 17 before the scheduled rotation. A verifier selecting slot B during revision 17 must load revision 17 before accepting callbacks.

references.title: Receipt callback retry policy
references.content: The provider retries callbacks after HTTP 5xx responses. Signature rejection returns HTTP 401 and is not retried because repeating the same signed callback cannot change the verification key.

incident.title: Order updates stop behind a database wait
incident.description: Order writes time out while guidance describes both connection scarcity and row-lock contention.

evidence.summary: Seven order updates are waiting on the same row lock owned by transaction 881.
Transaction 881 remains open and idle in transaction for 180 seconds.
One caller times out after waiting behind the blocked order updates.

references.title: Order row-lock incident guide
references.content: A shared blocking transaction ID across waiting order updates identifies row-lock contention. Confirm the lock owner and its transaction state. An idle transaction that retains the lock blocks later writers until it commits or rolls back. A downstream connection timeout can be an effect of the blocked work rather than proof that the connection pool is undersized.

incident.title: Report delivery fails

evidence.summary: Rendering completes and the upload request reaches object storage.

references.content: Object storage evaluates explicit deny rules before allow rules. An explicit deny on object creation prevents the uploader role from writing reports even if it also has an allow rule.
An exhausted renderer queue prevents rendering completion. A missing storage container returns NoSuchBucket, while a policy rejection returns AccessDenied.
